requirements.requirement: Record every command run through sudo to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: A global sudoers policy directs sudo logging to the required file and validates successfully. Pre- and post-restart sudo probes produced records containing timestamps, invoking user root, target user, and command; prior records persisted and new logging worked after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: Distinct sudo probes appeared in the dedicated log but were absent from /var/log/messages, /var/log/secure, and the system journal both before and after restart. The installed policy explicitly disables sudo syslog output.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged across execution and restart. The solution uses the installed sudo implementation, and visudo accepted the configuration before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the connection disruption was observed, the boot ID changed and independently matched lifecycle snapshots, and configuration, service state, prior log data, platform identity, and fresh isolated sudo logging recovered.
limitations: Behavioral probes used root as the invoking sudo user; coverage for other users is supported by the global Defaults policy rather than a separate non-root probe.
As with any bounded verification, the evidence samples representative sudo commands rather than exhaustively observing every possible future invocation.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The sudoers file installation was the required implementation; the two probe invocations created only required audit evidence; and the transient reboot unit and reboot were required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The temporary sudoers staging file was consumed by the atomic move, while the reboot unit was transient and absent after reboot. Final lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, new listening exposure, package damage, or abandoned temporary files beyond normal boot-specific systemd directories.
